summary: BLM lookout on Murphy Dome, about 20 mi NW of Fairbanks, was in use in 1970 per the BLM Alaska fire report; no source gives its build date, fate or site today.

facts.agency: Bureau of Land Management, Alaska State Office (per the 1970 Alaska Fire Report)
facts.status_note: No source after 1970 says whether the lookout stood, was removed or survives; sources describe the radar site on the summit, not the lookout

access.note: Most of the summit can be roamed, but the still-active radar facility is a restricted area; no source places the 1970 tower relative to it

events.note: In use as a lookout in 1970 (staffing not documented), one of two near Fairbanks (the other at Birch Hill)

notes_for_editor: Only one primary source names this lookout: the 1970 BLM Alaska Fire Report says lookout towers were in use 'at Murphy Dome' that year, and the report's date is October 1, 1970. The report does not say the tower was manned, only that it was in use, so staffing is recorded as 'in use; staffing not documented' for 1970 and the event as 'other', not as staffed. The GNIS point (64.95239, -148.35644) is the named summit, not a tower position, and the radar station (Murphy Dome AFS) occupies the same summit, so the tower's exact site is unknown. Sketches of Alaska describes the radar site only. No Forest Fire Lookout Association or NHLR record for this tower was found. Not checked: BLM Alaska Fire Service records and Fairbanks newspapers, which could give the build date, removal or current condition. No photo found.
